projects.title: This website — secure Flask portfolio with CI/CD
projects.summary: The site you are reading: a Python/Flask app with a two-factor-protected content editor, automated security testing and two deployment targets.
projects.details:
Content is edited in a private admin panel (password + two-factor login, CSRF protection, rate limiting, audit log) and stored as validated JSON.

Every push runs GitHub Actions: 44 unit and security tests, Bandit and pip-audit, CodeQL scanning and a Docker build. The same Flask code is then frozen into a static site and deployed to GitHub Pages with a strict Content-Security-Policy. For a custom domain it ships as a hardened container: non-root, read-only filesystem, gunicorn behind Caddy with automatic HTTPS.
results: No cookies, no trackers, strict CSP

projects.title: Multi-tier AWS environment with Terraform
projects.summary: A highly available multi-tier web environment on AWS, provisioned with reusable Terraform modules and variables.
projects.details:
Traffic enters through Route 53 and an Application Load Balancer that spreads requests across EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group inside a dedicated VPC. Application data is stored in Amazon RDS and static assets in S3, with access controlled by IAM roles.

The whole environment is described as Terraform code with reusable modules and variables, so it can be created, changed and destroyed reproducibly.

projects.title: Nine-stage Jenkins CI/CD pipeline
projects.summary: An end-to-end Jenkins pipeline for a rental-car application that connects Git, infrastructure provisioning, Docker image builds and deployment.
projects.details:
The pipeline turns every push into a reproducible delivery: the code is checked out, infrastructure is provisioned with Terraform, servers are configured with Ansible, the application is built into Docker images and pushed to a registry, and the new version is deployed.

Each stage is a separate, observable step, so a failure is easy to locate and the whole flow can be re-run from a clean state.
results: 9 automated stages from commit to deployment
Infrastructure and app delivered by one pipeline
Repeatable runs from a clean state

projects.title: OptiFaaS — benchmarking serverless platforms
projects.context: Research at TU Berlin · DFG project with TU Dortmund
projects.summary: Event-driven Java prototypes and benchmarking experiments for a research project on the optimal, adaptive placement of FaaS functions.
projects.details:
OptiFaaS is a DFG-funded research project of TU Berlin and TU Dortmund. It asks how Function-as-a-Service workloads can be placed and scheduled across cloud, edge and fog so that they meet their latency, cost and privacy goals, taking data locality and cold starts into account.

My part was the experimental side: I designed and developed event-driven, distributed software prototypes in Java, deployed them with Docker on Linux, AWS Lambda and Google Cloud Functions, and ran benchmarking experiments to measure scalability, concurrency and performance. I coordinated with the external project partners and onboarded and supervised a student research assistant.
results: Event-driven prototypes on two cloud FaaS platforms
